run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T12:57:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is supported by frontend-proxy's own error signals. frontend-proxy's errored spans are `ingress` spans with error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR, paired with child `router frontend egress` spans carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0" (no upstream response); the parent load-generator `GET` span also carries 503/ERROR. Its Envoy access logs name the mechanism exactly: `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against upstream cluster `frontend` for GET /api/products/*, /api/recommendations, /api/cart and GET /. The `frontend` Service has a single endpoint, pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw, so the upstream that terminates the connection before sending response headers is that frontend pod's application. The resets are chronic and low-rate: earliest matching log line 12:26:55, continuing through 13:05:06, i.e. ~30 minutes before the 12:57:01 alert start and after it, which fits an 'error rate above 0' alert rather than a step change. frontend records its own errored spans in the 12:53:01-12:59:01 readings (GET, POST, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, tcp.connect) and load-generator records 503s. No pod crashed, was evicted or OOMKilled: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0. The only cluster change in the window is a product-catalog Deployment rollout at 12:49:36-12:49:40 (new ReplicaSet, same image tag, old ReplicaSet scaled to 0), which I reject as this cause because the 503 resets predate it and product-catalog has no errored spans. The deepest supported cause is the single frontend pod terminating upstream connections; the in-application reason is not observable with the available telemetry.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span error rate is nonzero across the readable window, peaking at 0.0368 spans/s at 12:52:01 and easing to 0.0035-0.0070 spans/s from 13:01:01; by operation, `ingress` errors peak at 0.0246/s at 12:53:01 and `router frontend egress` errors at 0.0105/s in 12:53:01-12:59:01.

In frontend-proxy error traces, the `ingress` span of service frontend-proxy carries error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR and its child `router frontend egress` span carries error="true" and http.status_code="0"; the parent load-generator `GET` span carries error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR. No span of service frontend appears in the failed traces, so no call edge from frontend-proxy into frontend is proven by parent references.

frontend-proxy access logs record the exact failure mode: `"GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4 HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`, and the same 503 UC line for GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO, GET /api/recommendations?productIds=0PUK6V6EV0, GET /api/cart and GET /, each with upstream cluster name `frontend`. No 500/502/504 or `no healthy upstream`/UF lines were found in the window.

The `frontend` Service (ClusterIP 100.71.221.228, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend) has exactly one endpoint address, 100.96.3.42, whose targetRef is Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw. Pod IPs are frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw=100.96.3.42, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56=100.96.3.19 and load-generator-57ffcd644-bkb6s=100.96.3.52, matching the logs' `frontend 100.96.3.19:<ephemeral> ... 100.96.3.52:<ephemeral>` fields.

frontend records its own errored spans — GET 0.00877/s, POST 0.00175/s, POST /api/checkout 0.00175/s, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 0.00175/s and tcp.connect 0.00175/s — nonzero only in the readings 12:53:01, 12:55:01, 12:57:01 and 12:59:01 and zero before and after, against a total frontend span rate of ~45-48 spans/s (STATUS_CODE_UNSET).

All 21 otel-demo pods are phase Running, every PodReadyToStartContainers/Initialized/Ready/ContainersReady/PodScheduled condition is True, and every container has restartCount 0 with empty lastState (frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw started 12:16:37, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 started 12:16:38).

The only events in otel-demo within the window are the product-catalog rollout at 12:49:36-12:49:40: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet up product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1 and down product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, and Pod Killing 'Stopping container product-catalog'. No Evicted, OOMKilled, FailedScheduling or Unhealthy events exist.

product-catalog's Deployment is generation 2 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog unchanged; ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 was created 12:49:36 alongside product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc created 12:16:36 (now 0 replicas), and its pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 is Running with restartCount 0.

No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series exists for product-catalog, cart, checkout, currency, email, shipping, quote, image-provider or kafka in the window even though those services carry span traffic (increase over 40m: product-catalog 7564, cart 10630, checkout 5114, email 1507, shipping 1124, currency 1058); the only services with errored spans are frontend-proxy, frontend, ad, fraud-detection, recommendation, accounting and payment (the last two read 0).

frontend's container is limited to cpu 100m / memory 200Mi (requests 50m/100Mi) and has no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe; measured CPU usage is 0.0465-0.0499 cores throughout, the CFS-throttled fraction is 0.26-0.31 in every reading including the pre-alert baseline, and memory working set grows from 119672832 to 131420160 bytes.

The immediate cause of the RequestErrorRate alert is the upstream (Envoy cluster `frontend`, i.e. the single endpoint pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw) closing frontend-proxy's upstream connection before response headers (Envoy `UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`), so frontend-proxy returns 503 to load-generator. The specific in-application reason at frontend is not observable in the supplied telemetry.

A remaining candidate is frontend resource pressure: the pod runs at ~0.048 of its 100m CPU limit with 26-31% of CFS periods throttled and memory creeping toward the 200Mi limit, which could cause dropped in-flight requests. It does not track the 12:52-12:59 error peak (CPU 0.0475 at 12:49:01 vs 0.0498 at 12:53:01; throttle 0.28 vs 0.31), so it stays an unresolved contributor rather than an established cause.

A second remaining candidate is a failed outbound connection from frontend: frontend's own `tcp.connect` span records errors at 0.00175/s in the 12:53:01-12:59:01 readings, so at least one outbound TCP connect from frontend failed in that band and could have aborted request handling. The dependency targeted by that failed connect is not visible in the projected span fields.

Rejected: the product-catalog Deployment rollout at 12:49:36 caused this alert. frontend-proxy's 503 UC resets begin at 12:26:55, about 23 minutes before the rollout, and continue at 13:00:52-13:05:06 after it; product-catalog shows no STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series despite ~7564 spans/40m, and its new pod was created by its own ReplicaSet with restartCount 0 — a controller-driven replace, not damage.

Rejected: a crash, OOMKill, eviction or failed readiness of frontend or frontend-proxy. Both pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, the deployments report availableReplicas/readyReplicas 1 with Available and NewReplicaSetAvailable True, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/Unhealthy events exist in the window.

The ad, fraud-detection and recommendation error series are a separate constant background signal: each is exactly 0.0017543859649122805/s for the whole window and is attached to flagd-evaluation streaming operations (`flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` for ad and fraud-detection, `/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` for recommendation), unlike frontend-proxy's varying `ingress`/`router frontend egress` errors, so they do not account for the frontend-proxy alert.

Add readiness and liveness probes to the frontend Deployment: it currently has neither, so a frontend instance that resets connections stays in the `frontend` Service endpoints and keeps receiving frontend-proxy traffic.

Investigate the frontend application's connection handling for requests ending in `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` (unhandled rejections or aborted responses) and consider raising the 100m CPU limit given the sustained 26-31% CFS throttling; both are advisory and were not executed.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule's expression and threshold are not visible: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate (status no_data) and no alerting rules at all (status no_data), so the annotation value 0.01111111111111111 cannot be recomputed or compared with the observed span rates.

frontend produced no container log lines in the windows read (12:45:00-13:02:00 and 12:49:00-13:02:00 both returned status no_data with bytes_read 0), so there is no application-level error text explaining why it terminates connections.

Jaeger returned no frontend error traces for tags error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR or http.status_code=500 (all status no_data), so the status codes and details of frontend's errored GET/POST/tcp.connect spans remain unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so why product-catalog's Deployment reached generation 2 with a new ReplicaSet at 12:49:36 (same image tag) cannot be established; its pod-template diff is unverified.
rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count has no series for service_name=frontend (status no_data), so frontend's gRPC-level status codes toward its dependencies could not be verified.

frontend-proxy log reads hit stated limits: the 12:16-12:45 read was cut at the 4 MiB read limit (read through 12:45:57, view incomplete) and the later read ended at 13:06:05, so 503s outside those ranges are unknown.
The failed outbound `tcp.connect` span on frontend does not expose its target host, so the dependency involved cannot be named.
Whether the resets originate in the frontend application, its container networking or the node cannot be distinguished with the evidence available in this Run.

No pod-level resource-limit or readiness failure was observed, but the frontend pod's internal state (event-loop lag, HTTP keep-alive handling) has no metric series in this environment (nodejs_* metrics absent) and remains unmeasured.
next_steps: Have a human read the frontend pod's application stderr/stdout around 12:26-13:06 for unhandled errors and inspect the Next.js server instrumentation for aborted responses.
Locate and review the RequestErrorRate rule definition outside this Prometheus to confirm its numerator/denominator and whether a threshold above 0 is intended.
Check the frontend pod's node-level networking (conntrack drops, SYN backlog) and whether resets correlate with kube-proxy/CNI events.
Use the change-history source (not integrated here) to identify what changed in the product-catalog Deployment spec at 12:49:36.
